entries.title: Connectors: every MCP server, on both hosts
entries.body: A new tab after Skills finds every MCP server and connector Claude Code and Codex can use, checks which work, lists their tools and counts their calls over 30 days. What failed comes first with one fix, and the rail's badge counts it. Copy to … moved here from Skills. Add server adds one to either host or both, its secrets by name only; a server's sheet parks it (off, its settings kept for Turn on) or removes it.

entries.title: Files is a Finder for your vault
entries.body: Icons, List and Columns (⌃⌘1–3), with folder art, item counts and a tab of colour for brain, workspaces, persona and the daily notes. A click selects and a double-click opens; Space is Quick Look, ⇧⌘P the preview, and files that are not text open in their own app.

entries.title: Rename, move and undo, links included
entries.body: Return renames in place, drag moves a file or a selection onto any folder, and ⌘Z undoes the last move or rename. The notes that link to it are updated, so their links keep working; the runtime's own folders say why they refuse.

entries.title: Thumbnails, smart folders and tags
entries.body: Images show as pictures in Icons. The sidebar's Recents, Changed today and Images gather files from across the vault, Tags lists the notes under your most used tags, and Favorites take any folder you drag onto them.

entries.title: Search by name or inside, here or everywhere
entries.body: As you type in Files' search, a bar picks the whole vault or the folder you are in, and names (shown in the view, ready to open or drag) or the lines inside the files, each opening at its line.

entries.title: Background work on your Mac
entries.body: Session summaries, memory, workspace insights and file maps, recall, the Pulse briefing and the AI buttons run on a model on this Mac and never spend. When it can't answer, the work waits or uses heuristics; nothing falls back to a paid model unless you allow it. An install from before 2.0 is asked once, and Settings ▸ Local engine can go local or undo it later.

entries.title: Your Chief of Staff on Opus 5.5 or gpt-6-sol
entries.body: Its duties run on Claude Code · claude-opus-5-5 or Codex · gpt-6-sol, and with both hosts a duty that can't start on one moves to the other; an install from before 2.0 keeps its model until the Go-local card moves it. The hourly check triages on this Mac first, so a quiet hour costs nothing. With no host yet, Pulse says how to add one.

entries.title: Routines run where you choose
entries.body: A prompt routine names its engine: the model on this Mac (free, with a built-in agent that writes only where the routine says), Claude Code or Codex, each with its own model. A routine without one runs as before.

entries.title: Your Claude Code and Codex history
entries.body: Your CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md rules, Claude Code's memories, both hosts' MCP servers and your past sessions come into the vault, on the local model: an install from before 2.0 is asked once, and Settings ▸ Import (or `aos import`) brings them in any time. Imported memories wait in Brain ▸ Review, one batch per host, until you keep them.

entries.title: Sessions ▸ History
entries.body: Every Claude Code and Codex session on this Mac, by day and newest first, with its host, workspace and a one-line summary once the history import has digested it. Resume reopens one in a Code terminal on its own host.

entries.title: A guided tour, Getting started and Help
entries.body: Help (the ? at the rail's foot, or the app's Help menu; ⌘P lists the same) has the welcome tour, a tour of the tab you are on and this list. Each tab offers its own tour on your first visit, and Getting started ticks first steps as you do them.
